summary.text: Michael (Mike) Katz, a Republican pediatric critical care anesthesiologist, business owner and former Delaware state senator, lost the November 3, 2026 election for the U.S. Senate seat in Delaware to Chris Coons.
He served one term in the Delaware State Senate (2009-2013) as a Democrat, ran for U.S. Senate in 2024 as an Independent, and later registered as a Republican.

paragraphs.text: According to his Ballotpedia survey response, Mike Katz grew up in a working-class family and was the first man in his family to attend college.
He earned a medical degree and an MBA in international business from Georgetown University.

His campaign website says he came to Delaware in 1996 when he was recruited from Boston Children's Hospital to A.I. duPont Hospital for Children, and that he has practiced as a pediatric critical care anesthesiologist in the state for more than 20 years.

He is also a business owner; WHYY reports that he owns a commercial real estate company, and his campaign website says he has held leadership roles with the Medical Society of Delaware and the American Medical Association.
Katz was elected as a Democrat to Delaware State Senate District 4, north of Wilmington and including Greenville, Centreville and Hockessin, and served from 2009 to 2013.
In the State Senate he worked on legislation about lobbying reform, term limits and health care policy, and his campaign website also cites the creation of the Delaware Health Information Network.
In 2024 he ran for U.S. Senate as an Independent for the seat vacated by Tom Carper, losing to Lisa Blunt Rochester.
Katz won the September 15, 2026, Republican primary over John Shulli. He lives in Delaware with his wife, Trish, and, according to his campaign materials, they have three adult children.
During the campaign, he said he was running on lowering the cost of living, health care reform, term limits and fiscal accountability.
He received 36.4% of the vote to Chris Coons's 63.6%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
